summary: Moshoeshoe I International Airport is Lesotho's primary international gateway, named after King Moshoeshoe I, the 19th-century founder of the Basotho nation. Located about 20 km southeast of the capital Maseru near Mazenod, it serves as the main entry point for visitors to the landlocked mountain kingdom. The airport handles both domestic flights to other Lesotho airfields and regional connections, mainly to South Africa.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from Maseru city center?
A: The airport is approximately 20 km (12 miles) southeast of central Maseru, with a typical drive taking around 25-35 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Which airlines operate from Moshoeshoe I International Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by South African Airways and its low-cost partner FlySafair, along with smaller regional carriers operating flights mainly to Johannesburg and other South African destinations.

Q: Are there customs and immigration facilities for international arrivals?
A: Yes, the airport has full customs, immigration, and health screening facilities as Lesotho's main port of entry, though processing times are generally quick given the moderate traffic volume.

Q: Is the airport open 24 hours?
A: Operating hours are limited and tied to scheduled flight arrivals and departures, so the terminal is generally not open overnight.
transport_tips: Taxis are the most common way to reach Maseru; agree on a fare before departure as meters are rarely used. Shared shuttle services and hotel pickups can sometimes be arranged in advance through your accommodation. Note that the main road to Maseru crosses into South Africa briefly in some routing options, so carry your passport if walking or driving near border areas.
